topic.name: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Repeated Eigenvalues

question.text: Find the general solution to the matrix differential equation $\, \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{3}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & -\dfrac{3}{4} \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}(t).$
question.explanation:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

\[ \begin{bmatrix} x'_1(t) \\ x'_2(t) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} {\lambda} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1(t) \\ x_2(t) \end{bmatrix}, \] the formula for the general solution is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} e^{\lambda t} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{\lambda t}, \qquad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Since the matrix of our differential equation is diagonal, the system is decoupled.

Therefore, the general solution is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} e^{-3t/4} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{-3t/4}, \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

example.title: Finding the General Solution to a System of Linear Equations in a Complete Case

question.text:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2\\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t). \]

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

\[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ a \end{bmatrix}e^{5 t} + c_2 \left( \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ a \end{bmatrix}te^{5 t} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ b \end{bmatrix}e^{5 t}\right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}, \]

what is the value of $a+b?$
question.explanation:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2\\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}.$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=5$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get \[ A - \lambda I = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \] So, we get an eigenvector $ \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. $

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t} + c_2 (\mathbf{v} te^{\lambda t} + \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ), \] where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

\begin{align} (A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} & = \mathbf{v}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 5 -5 & 2\\ 0 & 5-5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \end{align}

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rl} 0 w_1+ 2 w_2 = 1 \\[3pt] 0 w_1+ 0 w_2 = 0 \end{array} \right. \]

So, we obtain \[ w_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}. \]

The variable $w_1$ is a free variable. Setting $ w_1 = 0,$ we get \[ \mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, the general solution is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix}1\\ \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{0} \end{bmatrix}e^{5 t} + c_2 \left(\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{0} \end{bmatrix}t e^{5 t} + \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{\frac{1}{2}} \end{bmatrix}e^{5 t}\right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Finally, we see that $a=0, b=\dfrac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=\dfrac{1}{2}.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to a System of Linear Equations in a Defective Case

question.explanation:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-2$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get \[ A - \lambda I = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \] So, we get an eigenvector $ \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. $

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t} + c_2 (\mathbf{v}t e^{\lambda t} + \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t}), \] where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

\begin{align} (A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} & = \mathbf{v}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -2+2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2+2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \end{align}

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rl} 0 w_1 + 0 w_2 = 0 \\[3pt] 5 w_1 + 0 w_2 = 1 \end{array} \right. \]

So, we obtain \[ w_1 =\dfrac{1}{5}. \]

The variable $w_2$ is a free variable. Setting $ w_2 = 0,$ we get \[ \mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{5} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, the general solution is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t} + c_2 \left( \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}t e^{-2t} + \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{5} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t} \right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial condition $\mathbf{x}(0) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} .$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives \begin{align} \textbf{x}(0) & = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{c_2}{5} \\ c_1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{c_2}{5} \\ c_1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} . \end{align}

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by \begin{align} \mathbf{x}(t) &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}t e^{-2t} +\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t} .\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}t e^{-2t} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} e^{-2t} \\(2+ 5 t)e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}. \end{align}

example.title: Solving an Initial Value Problem in a Defective Case

question.text:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0\\ 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t). \]

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

\[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} a \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{- t} + c_2 \left( \begin{bmatrix} a \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}t e^{- t} + \begin{bmatrix} b \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{- t}\right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}, \]

what is the value of $a+b?$
question.explanation:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-1$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get \[ A - \lambda I = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \] So, we get an eigenvector $ \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. $

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t} + c_2 (\mathbf{v} t e^{\lambda t} + \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ), \] where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

\begin{align} (A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} & = \mathbf{v}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -1 - (-1)& 0 \\ 3 & -1 - (-1) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \end{align}

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rl} 0w_1+0 w_2 = 0 \\[3pt] 3 w_1+ 0 w_2 = 1 \end{array} \right. \]

So, we obtain \[ w_1 = \dfrac{1}{3}. \]

The variable $w_2$ is a free variable. Setting $ w_2 = 0,$ we get \[ \mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{3} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, the general solution is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{0} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{- t} + c_2 \left(\begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{0} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}t e^{- t} + \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{\dfrac{1}{3}} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{- t}\right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Finally, we see that $a=0, b=\dfrac{1}{3},$ and $a+b=\dfrac{1}{3}.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to a System of Linear Equations in a Defective Case

question.explanation:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & -6 \\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-3$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get \[ A - \lambda I = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \] So, we get an eigenvector $ \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. $

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t} + c_2 (\mathbf{v}t e^{\lambda t} + \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t}), \] where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

\begin{align} (A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} & = \mathbf{v}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -3 -(-3) & -6 \\ 0 & -3 -(-3) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -6\\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} w_1 \\ w_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \end{align}

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rl} 0 w_1 - 6 w_2 = 1 \\[3pt] 0 w_1 + 0 w_2 = 0 \end{array} \right. \]

So, we obtain \[ w_2 = -\dfrac{1}{6}. \]

The variable $w_1$ is a free variable. Setting $ w_1 = 0,$ we get \[ \mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -\frac{1}{6} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, the general solution is given by \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{-3t} + c_2 \left( \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}t e^{-3t} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -\frac{1}{6} \end{bmatrix}e^{-3t} \right), \quad c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}. \]

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial condition $\mathbf{x}(0) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} .$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives \begin{align} \textbf{x}(0) & = \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ -\dfrac{c_2}{6}\end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ -\dfrac{c_2}{6} \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{bmatrix} & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix} . \end{align}

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by \begin{align} \mathbf{x}(t) &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{-3t} + \begin{bmatrix} -12 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}t e^{-3t} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}e^{-3t} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} e^{-3t} + \begin{bmatrix} -12 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} t e^{-3t} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} (1-12t) e^{-3t} \\ 2\, e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix} . \end{align}
